mutant.description: Three readers had to be able to go either way, and all three were shown to. (1) AC4's strong-read instrument, run as a POSITIVE CONTROL against the one principal that does exist in the live table -- the arm AC4 itself cannot reach because no controlled principal key is constructible. (2) AC6's scanner, which produced a real FAIL and a PASS only after the cause was removed. (3) AC2's AWS shim path, which failed loudly rather than passing silently.
mutant.expected: (1) the reader returns a present record for an existing principal, proving AC4's FAIL is a true absence rather than a blind reader; (2) AC6 FAILs while a forbidden-shaped value is present and PASSes once it is gone; (3) a broken instrument is reported as a FAIL naming its cause.
mutant.observed: (1) 'rc=0 / items read: 3 / principal_profile found: 1 -> status=active' against an EXISTING principal -- the instrument CAN see a present record, so AC4's FAIL is a true absence. (2) AC6 fired for real TWICE and passed only after each cause was removed: first on the probe's own all-zero GUID sentinel (GUIDs are now blanked before the digit scan), then on a git commit hash cited in the record -- a digit-only lookaround treats the 9-digit tail of a hash beginning with a hex letter as an account number, so the boundary was widened to word-class. A negative control confirms the widened pattern STILL matches a standalone 10-digit token and a quoted one, and no longer matches a commit-ish. (3) AC2 returned rc=255 OSError('%1 is not a valid Win32 application') against the bash .tools/aws shim before the .cmd forwarder was resolved -- a FAIL with its cause, never a silent pass. (4) AMENDMENT A3's account count went both ways too: the first run RAISED ArrowInvalid('No match for FieldRef.Name(account_ref)') rather than counting the wrong column, which is how the contract-name / physical-column split (account_ref is a keyed HMAC over account_id, app/integrations/schwab/datasets.json:12) was found instead of silently miscounted.
